answer: A harbor underwrites each operator as a single liability: every non-empty subset of its identities can file a correlated claim, so an operator holding k identities must keep \(2^k-1\) quartz locked in one vault while any operates. Ten identities lock 1023 quartz; one identity locks one quartz. The harbor writes that liability against the operator's signed record and carries its head-count into any replacement, so a new vault cannot reset the balance.
